statements.subject: session
statements.description: A session is created when end-to-end PPP connection is attempted between a dial user and the PNS.
statements.trigger: PPP connection attempted between dial user and PNS

statements.subject: session
statements.description: PPTP is connection-oriented. The PNS and PAC maintain state for each user that is attached to a PAC.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Before PPP tunneling can occur between a PAC and PNS, a control connection must be established between them.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Following the establishment of the required TCP connection, the PNS and PAC establish the control connection using the Start-Control-Connection-Request and -Reply messages.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Once the control connection is established, the PAC or PNS may initiate sessions by requesting outbound calls or responding to inbound requests.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Following the establishment of the required TCP connection, the PNS and PAC establish the control connection using the Start-Control-Connection-Request and -Reply messages.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The PNS and PAC establish the control connection using the Start-Control-Connection-Request and -Reply messages. These messages are also used to exchange information about basic operating capabilities of the PAC and PNS.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The control connection itself is maintained by keep-alive echo messages. This ensures that a connectivity failure between the PNS and the PAC can be detected in a timely manner.
actions: detect connectivity failure via keep-alive echo timeout

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Before PPP tunneling can occur between a PAC and PNS, a control connection must be established between them.
actions: establish control connection between PAC and PNS

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: Once the control connection is established, the PAC or PNS may initiate sessions by requesting outbound calls or responding to inbound requests.
actions: initiate session by requesting outbound call
initiate session by responding to inbound request

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The control connection may communicate changes in operating characteristics of an individual user session with a Set-Link-Info message.
actions: send Set-Link-Info message on control connection

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Individual sessions may be released by either the PAC or PNS, also through Control Connection messages.
actions: send Control Connection message to release session

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: PPTP requires the establishment of a tunnel for each communicating PNS-PAC pair. This tunnel is used to carry all user session PPP packets for sessions involving a given PNS-PAC pair.
actions: establish GRE tunnel between PNS-PAC pair

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The value to use in the key field is established by the call establishment procedure which takes place on the control connection.
statements.trigger: call establishment procedure completes on control connection
actions: assign GRE key field value for session

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The control connection is used to determine rate and buffering parameters that are used to regulate the flow of PPP packets for a particular session over the tunnel.
statements.trigger: session flow parameters negotiated on control connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Loss of synchronization must result in immediate closing of the control connection's TCP session.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The control connection is initiated by either the PNS or PAC after they establish the underlying TCP connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Start-Control-Connection-Request is a PPTP control message used to establish the control connection between a PNS and a PAC. The establishment of the control connection can be initiated by either the PNS or PAC.
actions: initiate control connection establishment between PNS and PAC

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A control connection must be established before any other PPTP messages can be issued.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Start-Control-Connection-Reply is a PPTP control message sent in reply to a received Start-Control-Connection-Request message. This message contains a result code indicating the result of the control connection establishment attempt.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 1 - Successful channel establishment

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 2 - General error -- Error Code indicates the problem

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 3 - Command channel already exists

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 4 - Requester is not authorized to establish a command channel
actions: abort control channel establishment due to authorization failure

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 5 - The protocol version of the requester is not supported
actions: abort control channel establishment due to version mismatch

statements.subject: message
statements.description: In a Start-Control-Connection-Reply issued by the PNS, this value SHOULD be set to 0 and it must be ignored by the PAC.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: The Stop-Control-Connection-Request is a PPTP control message sent by one peer of a PAC-PNS control connection to inform the other peer that the control connection should be closed. In addition to closing the control connection, all active user calls are implicitly cleared.
actions: implicitly clear all active user calls

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: The Stop-Control-Connection-Reply is a PPTP control message sent by one peer of a PAC-PNS control connection upon receipt of a Stop-Control-Connection-Request from the other peer.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 1 (OK) - Control connection closed. Indicates the result of the attempt to close the control connection.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Result Code 2 (General Error) - Control connection not closed for reason indicated in Error Code.
actions: report general error from Error Code field

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: The receiving peer issues an Echo-Reply to each Echo-Request received.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the sender does not receive an Echo-Reply in response to an Echo-Request, it will eventually clear the control connection.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Outgoing-Call-Reply is a PPTP control message sent by the PAC to the PNS in response to a received Outgoing-Call-Request message. The reply indicates the result of the outgoing call attempt.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 1 (Connected) - Call established with no errors

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 2 (General Error) - Outgoing Call not established for the reason indicated in Error Code

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 3 (No Carrier) - Outgoing Call failed due to no carrier detected

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 4 (Busy) - Outgoing Call failed due to detection of a busy signal

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 5 (No Dial Tone) - Outgoing Call failed due to lack of a dial tone

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 6 (Time-out) - Outgoing Call was not established within time allotted by PAC

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 7 (Do Not Accept) - Outgoing Call administratively prohibited

statements.subject: server
statements.description: This value should be set to the maximum delay that can normally occur between the time a packet arrives at the PAC and is delivered to the client.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Incoming-Call-Request is a PPTP control message sent by the PAC to the PNS to indicate that an inbound call is to be established from the PAC. This message is the first in the 'three-way handshake' used by PPTP for establishing incoming calls.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PAC may defer answering the call until it has received an Incoming-Call-Reply from the PNS indicating that the call should be established. This mechanism allows the PNS to obtain sufficient information about the call before it is answered to determine whether the call should be answered or not.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Incoming-Call-Reply is the second message in the three-way handshake used by PPTP for establishing incoming calls. It indicates to the PAC whether the call should be answered or not.
actions: PNS sends Incoming-Call-Reply to PAC in response to Incoming-Call-Request

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Result Code 3 (Do Not Accept) - The PAC should not accept the incoming call. It should hang up or issue a busy indication.
statements.trigger: Incoming-Call-Reply received with Result Code = 3 (Do Not Accept)
actions: PAC hangs up incoming call or issues busy indication

statements.subject: server
statements.description: 1 (Connect) - The PAC should answer the incoming call

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 2 (General Error) - The Incoming Call should not be established due to the reason indicated in Error Code
statements.trigger: Incoming-Call-Reply received with Result Code = 2 (General Error)

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: 3 (Do Not Accept) - The PAC should not accept the incoming call. It should hang up or issue a busy indication.

actions: Hang up or issue a busy indication

statements.subject: peer
statements.trigger: Result Code = 3 (Do Not Accept) in Incoming-Call-Reply

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Call-Clear-Request is a PPTP control message sent by the PNS to the PAC indicating that a particular call is to be disconnected. The call being cleared can be either an incoming or outgoing call, in any state. The PAC responds to this message with a Call-Disconnect-Notify message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The Call-Disconnect-Notify message is a PPTP control message sent by the PAC to the PNS. It is issued whenever a call is disconnected, due to the receipt by the PAC of a Call-Clear-Request or for any other reason. Its purpose is to inform the PNS of both the disconnection and the reason for it.
actions: send Call-Disconnect-Notify from PAC to PNS

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 4 (Request) - Call disconnected due to received Call-Clear-Request
actions: send Call-Disconnect-Notify with Result Code 4 from PAC to PNS

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 1 (Lost Carrier) - Call disconnected due to loss of carrier
statements.trigger: loss of carrier detected by PAC
actions: send Call-Disconnect-Notify with Result Code 1 from PAC to PNS

statements.subject: session
statements.description: 3 (Admin Shutdown) - Call disconnected for administrative reasons
actions: send Call-Disconnect-Notify with Result Code 3 from PAC to PNS

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: This message should only be sent when an error occurs, and not more than once every 60 seconds.

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: Because these options can change at any time during the life of the call, the PAC must be able to update its internal call information dynamically and perform PPP negotiation on an active PPP session.
actions: perform PPP negotiation on the active PPP session

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: If a PPTP reply indicates in its Result Code that a general error occurred, the General Error value should be examined to determined what the error was.
actions: examine General Error field of reply to determine specific error cause

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If an expected reply does not arrive within 60 seconds, the control connection is closed, unless otherwise specified.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: restarted to ensure recovery into a known state

actions: initiate error recovery mechanism upon TCP connection closure

statements.subject: connection

actions: log receipt of invalid or malformed Control Connection message

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: idle - The control connection originator attempts to open a TCP connection to the peer during idle state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: wait_ctl_reply - The originator checks to see if another TCP connection has been requested from the same peer, and if so, handles the collision situation described in section 3.1.3.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: established - An established connection may be terminated by either a local condition or the receipt of a Stop-Control-Connection-Request.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: wait_stop_reply - If a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply is received, the TCP connection SHOULD be closed and the control connection becomes idle.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: TCP Open Indication / Send Start Control Connection Request: when the TCP connection is open, the originator transmits a Start-Control-Connection-Request and then enters the wait_ctl_reply state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Collision/See (4.1.3) Close TCP: originator moves from wait_ctl_reply back to idle when a collision is detected.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Receive Start-Control-Connection-Reply, Version OK: if the version in the reply is earlier and supported, the originator moves to the established state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Receive Stop-Control-Connection-Reply / Close TCP: originator moves from wait_stop_reply to idle.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the version of the reply is lower than the version sent in the request, the older (lower) version should be used provided it is supported.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Reply received with lower supported version
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = wait_ctl_reply & reply.version < request.version & reply.version.supported = true
actions: Use the older (lower) version from the reply

statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Reply received with unsupported earlier version
statements.pre_cond: protocol.state = wait_ctl_reply & reply.version < request.version & reply.version.supported = false

statements.description: In the event of a local termination, the originator MUST send a Stop-Control-Connection-Request and enter the wait_stop_reply state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If the originator receives a Stop-Control-Connection-Request it SHOULD send a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply and close the TCP connection making sure that the final TCP information has been "pushed" properly.
statements.post_cond: protocol.state = idle & tcp.connection = closed & tcp.data_pushed = true
actions: Ensure final TCP information is pushed properly

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: If a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply is received, the TCP connection SHOULD be closed and the control connection becomes idle.
actions: Transition control connection to idle state

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: idle: The control connection receiver waits for a TCP open attempt on port 1723.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: established: An established connection may be terminated by either a local condition or the reception of a Stop-Control-Connection-Request.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: wait_stop_reply: If a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply is received, the TCP connection SHOULD be closed and the control connection becomes idle.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Version Not OK / Send Start Control Connection Reply with Error; remain in Idle. If the version cannot be supported, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Connection-Reply message, close the TCP connection and remain in the idle state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Receive Start Ctl Connection Request / Send Stop Reply, Close TCP; return to Idle. (State diagram label; prose specifies this trigger as Stop-Control-Connection-Request.)

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Local Terminate / Send Stop Control Connection Request; enter Wait-Stop-Reply. In the event of a local termination, the originator MUST send a Stop-Control-Connection-Request and enter the wait_stop_reply state.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: Receive Stop Control Connection Reply / Close TCP; control connection becomes idle. If a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply is received, the TCP connection SHOULD be closed and the control connection becomes idle.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the version is earlier than the receiver's version and the earlier version can be supported by the receiver, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Control-Connection-Reply.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Request received with earlier but supported version

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the version is earlier than the receiver's version and the version cannot be supported, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Connection-Reply message, close the TCP connection and remain in the idle state.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Request received with unsupported earlier version
statements.pre_cond: receiver.state = idle & received.version < receiver.version & receiver.supports(received.version) = false

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the receiver's version is the same as earlier than the peer's, the receiver SHOULD send a Start-Control-Connection-Reply with the receiver's version and enter the established state.

statements.subject: endpoint
statements.description: If the originator receives a Stop-Control-Connection-Request it SHOULD send a Stop-Control-Connection-Reply and close the TCP connection, making sure that the final TCP information has been "pushed" properly.
actions: ensure final TCP data is pushed

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: When a Start-Control-Connection-Request is received on one TCP connection and another Start-Control-Connection-Request has already been sent on another TCP connection to the same peer, a collision has occurred.
statements.trigger: Start-Control-Connection-Request received while Start-Control-Connection-Request already sent to same peer
actions: determine winner by higher IP address (32-bit unsigned comparison, network number more significant)

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: The loser will immediately close the TCP connection it initiated, without sending any further PPTP control messages on it and will respond to the winner's request with a Start-Control-Connection-Reply message.
statements.trigger: collision resolution: local IP address < remote IP address
actions: send no further PPTP control messages on initiated connection

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: The winner will wait for the Start-Control-Connection-Reply on the connection it initiated and also wait for a TCP termination indication on the connection the loser opened. The winner MUST NOT send any messages on the connection the loser initiated.
statements.trigger: collision resolution: local IP address > remote IP address
actions: wait for Start-Control-Connection-Reply on initiated connection
wait for TCP termination indication on loser's connection
send no messages on loser's connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A PAC and PNS must have only one control connection between them.
actions: enforce single control connection per PAC-PNS pair

statements.subject: participant
statements.description: The winner MUST NOT send any messages on the connection the loser initiated.
actions: suppress all outbound PPTP control messages on loser-initiated TCP connection

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A control connection is in the established state when Start-Control-Connection-Request and Start-Control-Connection-Reply have been exchanged.

statements.subject: connection
statements.description: A control connection SHOULD be closed by closing the underlying TCP connection under the following circumstances:

statements.pre_cond: connection.state != established & (Start-Control-Connection-Request.received = false | Start-Control-Connection-Reply.received = false) & timer.elapsed >= 60

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: If a peer's control connection is in the established state and has not received a control message for 60 seconds, it SHOULD send a Echo-Request message.

statements.pre_cond: connection.state = established & Echo-Request.sent = true & Echo-Reply.received = false & timer.echo_elapsed >= 60
actions: close control connection by closing underlying TCP connection

statements.description: connections in the idle or established states

statements.description: If the PNS chooses to accept the call, it responds with an Incoming-Call-Reply which also indicates window sizes.

statements.description: When the PAC receives the Outgoing-Call-Reply, it attempts to connect the call, assuming the calling party has not hung up.

statements.description: When the dialed-in client hangs up, the call is cleared normally and the PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message.

statements.description: If the PNS wishes to clear a call, it sends a Call-Clear-Request message and then waits for a Call-Disconnect-Notify.

statements.subject: server

statements.pre_cond: pns.resources.available = false | pns.address.authorized = false | pns.bearer_service.authorized = false

statements.subject: session
statements.description: A final call connected message from the PAC to the PNS indicates that the call states for both the PAC and the PNS should enter the established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: idle: The PAC detects an incoming call on one of its telco interfaces. The PAC sends an Incoming-Call-Request message and moves to the wait_reply state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: wait_reply: The PAC receives an Incoming-Call-Reply message indicating non-willingness to accept the call and moves back into the idle state. If the reply message indicates that the call is accepted, the PAC sends an Incoming-Call-Connected message and enters the established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: established: Data is exchanged over the tunnel. The call may be cleared following an event on the telco connection, receipt of a Call-Clear-Request, or a local reason.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Ring/Send Incoming Call Request: PAC detects incoming call, sends Incoming-Call-Request and moves to wait_reply state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Incoming Call Reply Not Accepting: PAC receives Incoming-Call-Reply indicating non-willingness to accept and moves back to idle.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Abort/Send Call Disconnect Notify from wait_reply back to idle.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Incoming Call Reply Accepting/Answer call; Send Call Connected: PAC answers the call and sends Incoming-Call-Connected, entering established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Clear Call Request or telco call dropped or local disconnect/Send Call Disconnect Notify: PAC transitions from established back to idle.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The call may be cleared following: An event on the telco connection. The PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message Receipt of a Call-Clear-Request.  The PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message A local reason. The PAC sends a Call-Disconnect-Notify message.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: idle - An Incoming-Call-Request message is received. If the request is not acceptable, an Incoming-Call-Reply is sent back to the PAC and the PNS remains in the idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: wait_connect - If the session is connected on the PAC, the PAC sends an incoming call connect message to the PNS which then moves into established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: established - The session is terminated either by receipt of a Call-Disconnect-Notify message from the PAC or by sending a Call-Clear-Request.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: wait_disconnect - Once a Call-Disconnect-Notify is received the session moves back to the idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Incoming-Call-Request message is not acceptable, an Incoming-Call-Reply is sent back to the PAC and the PNS remains in the idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the Incoming-Call-Request message is acceptable, an Incoming-Call-Reply is sent indicating accept in the result code. The session moves to the wait_connect state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the session is connected on the PAC, the PAC sends an incoming call connect message to the PNS which then moves into established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session is terminated by receipt of a Call-Disconnect-Notify message from the PAC; session moves from established to idle.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The session is terminated by sending a Call-Clear-Request. Once a Call-Clear-Request has been sent, the session enters the wait_disconnect state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once a Call-Disconnect-Notify is received the session moves back to the idle state.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PAC may send a Call-Disconnect-Notify to indicate that the incoming caller could not be connected.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PNS sends an Outgoing-Call-Request specifying the dialed party phone number and subaddress as well as speed and window parameters.

statements.subject: server
statements.description: The PAC MUST respond to the Outgoing-Call-Request message with an Outgoing-Call-Reply message once the PAC determines that: The call has been successfully connected A call failure has occurred for reasons such as: no interfaces are available for dial-out, the called party is busy or does not answer, or no dial tone is detected on the interface chosen for dialing

statements.subject: session
statements.description: idle: Received Outgoing-Call-Request. If this is received in error, respond with an Outgoing-Call-Reply with error condition set. Otherwise, allocate physical channel to dial on. Place the outbound call, wait for a connection, and move to the wait_cs_ans state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: wait_cs_ans: If the call is incomplete, send an Outgoing-Call-Reply with a non-zero Error Code. If a timer expires on an outbound call, send back an Outgoing-Call-Reply with a non-zero Error Code. If a circuit switched connection is established, send an Outgoing-Call-Reply indicating success.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: established: If a Call-Clear-Request is received, the telco call SHOULD be released via appropriate mechanisms and a Call-Disconnect-Notify message SHOULD BE sent to the PNS. If the call is disconnected by the client or by the telco interface, a Call-Disconnect-Notify message SHOULD be sent to the PNS.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Outgoing Call Request in Error / Send Outgoing Call Reply with Error (self-loop on idle)
actions: Send Outgoing-Call-Reply with error condition set

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Outgoing Call Request No Error / Off Hook; Dial -> move to wait_cs_ans

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Incomplete Call / Send Outgoing Call Reply with Error -> return to idle
actions: Send Outgoing-Call-Reply with non-zero Error Code

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Recv. Call Clear Req. / Send Disconnect Notify -> return to idle from wait_cs_ans

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Telco Answer / Send Outgoing Call Reply -> move to established

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Call Clear Request or local terminate or telco disconnect / Hangup call and send Call Disconnect Notify -> return to idle
statements.trigger: Receive Call-Clear-Request or local terminate or telco disconnect
actions: release telco call via appropriate mechanisms

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a Call-Clear-Request is received, the telco call SHOULD be released via appropriate mechanisms and a Call-Disconnect-Notify message SHOULD BE sent to the PNS.
actions: Release telco call via appropriate mechanisms

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If the call is disconnected by the client or by the telco interface, a Call-Disconnect-Notify message SHOULD be sent to the PNS.
statements.trigger: call disconnected by client or telco interface

statements.subject: session
statements.description: idle - An Outgoing-Call-Request message is sent to the PAC and the session moves into the wait_reply state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: wait_reply - An Outgoing-Call-Reply is received which indicates an error. The session returns to idle state. No telco call is active. If the Outgoing-Call-Reply does not indicate an error, the telco call is connected and the session moves to the established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: established - If a Call-Disconnect-Notify is received, the telco call has been terminated for the reason indicated in the Result and Cause Codes. The session moves back to the idle state. If the PNS chooses to terminate the session, it sends a Call-Clear-Request to the PAC and then enters the wait_disconnect state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: wait_disconnect - A session disconnection is waiting to be confirmed by the PAC. Once the PNS receives the Call-Disconnect-Notify message, the session enters idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Open Indication / Send Outgoing Call Request: session moves from idle to wait_reply

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Outgoing Call Reply with Error: session returns to idle state. No telco call is active.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Receive Outgoing Call Reply No Error: the telco call is connected and the session moves to the established state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Abort/Send Call Clear Request from wait_reply: session transitions to wait_disconnect.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: If a Call-Disconnect-Notify is received in established state, the telco call has been terminated and the session moves back to the idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Local Terminate / Send Call Clear Request: If the PNS chooses to terminate the session, it sends a Call-Clear-Request to the PAC and then enters the wait_disconnect state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: Once the PNS receives the Call-Disconnect-Notify message in wait_disconnect, the session enters idle state.

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The sequence number for each user session is set to zero at session startup.
actions: initialize session sequence number to zero

statements.subject: peer
statements.description: When the PAC does receive packet 3, it MUST not attempt to transmit it to the corresponding PPP client.
actions: do not forward out-of-sequence GRE packet to PPP client

statements.subject: message
statements.description: PPP does properly deal with the loss of packets, but not with reordering so out of sequence packets between the PNS and PAC MUST be silently discarded, or they may be reordered by the receiver.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Adaptive Time-Out (ATO) is the time that must elapse before an acknowledgment is considered lost. After a time-out, the sliding window is partially closed and the ATO is backed off.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Timer backoff is done every time an acknowledgment time-out occurs. The backed-off timer value is limited by the configurable maximum time-out value.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: PPTP requires that a time-out be used to recover from dropped data or acknowledgment packets.
actions: use time-out to recover from dropped data or acknowledgment packets

statements.subject: session
statements.description: The PPD must be exchanged in the call connect sequences, even if it remains constant in an implementation.
actions: exchange PPD parameter during call connect sequences

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: When a time-out occurs, the time-out value should be adjusted rapidly upward.

statements.subject: timer
statements.description: Although the GRE packets are not retransmitted when a time-out occurs, the time-out should be adjusted up toward a maximum limit.

statements.subject: pptp
statements.description: To compensate for shifting internetwork time delays, a strategy must be employed to increase the time-out when it expires (notice that in addition to increasing the time-out, we are also shrinking the size of the window as described in the next section).
